acceptance_criteria.criterion: The DiffWindow displays a recommendations sidebar to the right of the diff list when differences are detected, with the diff list and sidebar sharing the content area via a two-column Grid.

The sidebar shows a "Removed Mods — High Risk" card with red styling (`DiffBrush.GuidanceRemovalBackground`) and `AlertCircleOutline` icon when `ShowRemovalGuidance` is true, with heading, count subtitle, and body text bindings.

The sidebar shows an "Inserted Mods — Moderate Risk" card with orange styling (`DiffBrush.GuidanceInsertionBackground`) when `ShowInsertionGuidance` is true, with heading, count subtitle, and body text bindings.
The sidebar shows a "Replaced Mods — Safe" card with purple styling (`DiffBrush.GuidanceReplacementBackground`) when `ShowReplacementGuidance` is true.
The sidebar shows a "New Mods — Safe" card with green styling (`DiffBrush.GuidanceAddedBackground`) when `ShowAddedGuidance` is true.
The sidebar shows a "No Changes" card when `ShowNoChangesGuidance` is true.
Cards appear and disappear dynamically based on `Show*Guidance` visibility bindings using `BooleanToVisibilityConverter`.
The default window width is `1060` and `MinWidth` is `720`, preserving diff list readability at the new dimensions.
The sidebar does not interfere with the existing sorting recommendation banner (Grid.Row="3"), button row (Grid.Row="6"), or `ConfigInvalidOverlay` (`Panel.ZIndex="1000"`).
All text bindings use ViewModel pass-through properties (e.g., `{Binding GuidanceRemovalTitle}`), not `Texts.*` sub-paths.
Cards use `materialDesign:Card` controls with `UniformCornerRadius="8"` for semantic card rendering.

summary: Restructured DiffWindow.xaml Grid.Row=2 from a single Border+ListView into a two-column Grid. Column 0 (star-sized) holds the existing diff list inside its original Border. Column 1 (260px fixed) holds a new sidebar Border containing a ScrollViewer+StackPanel with a title TextBlock and five materialDesign:Card elements (Removal, Insertion, Replacement, Added, No Changes). All cards use UniformCornerRadius=8, visibility bound via BooleanToVisibilityConverter to Show*Guidance properties, DiffBrush.Guidance*Background brushes, PackIcon with risk-coded icon and color, heading TextBlock bound to Guidance*Title, count subtitle bound to *ModCountText (except No Changes), and body TextBlock bound to Guidance*Body. Window Width changed 810→1060, MinWidth changed 480→720. All existing rows (0,1,3,4,5,6) and the ConfigInvalidOverlay at Panel.ZIndex=1000 are untouched. Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Tests: 492 pass, 0 fail, 2 pre-existing skips.

comments.note: The sidebar Border uses BorderThickness=0 and a semi-transparent GuidanceSidebarBackground brush. A subtle left-edge divider (BorderThickness="1,0,0,0" with MaterialDesignDivider) could visually separate the sidebar from the diff list more clearly without relying solely on the background color difference — useful in high-contrast or dark themes where the semi-transparent brush may be nearly invisible.

The diff list Border (column 0) closes its tag two indent levels below the opening tag without an intermediate blank line, creating a minor readability inconsistency vs. the sidebar Border directly below it. Cosmetic only; no functional impact.

AC-01: Two-column Grid in Row=2 confirmed (columns: *, 260). Edge case — Moved-only diff: ShowNoChangesGuidance=false, all 4 change-type cards hidden → sidebar shows title only. Accepted design gap per plan (sorting banner covers this scenario).
Edge case — MinWidth=720: diff list effective width ~452px at minimum, accepted per WP rationale.
Edge case — empty collection: ShowNoChangesGuidance=true, No Changes card appears. Correct.
Edge case — ConfigInvalidOverlay: confirmed root-Grid-level placement with ZIndex=1000 covers DockPanel+sidebar.

comments.note: Moved-only diff edge case: when diff contains only DiffChangeType.Moved entries, HasDifferences=true but all 4 change-type guidance cards are hidden and ShowNoChangesGuidance=false, leaving the sidebar with title text only and no cards. This is an acknowledged design gap per the API surface documentation — the sorting recommendation banner covers this scenario. No action required.

The No Changes card (lines 489–512) has no explicit Background binding — it inherits the MaterialDesign card default. This is visually fine, but a dedicated DiffBrush.GuidanceNoChangesBackground brush would make the intent explicit and allow independent theming in a future dark/high-contrast pass. Low priority; no functional impact.

The sidebar Border uses BorderThickness=0 with no visible separator from the diff list. At MinWidth=720, the diff list narrows to ~452px effective width. A 1px left-edge divider (MaterialDesignDivider brush) would improve clarity, especially in high-contrast or dark themes where GuidanceSidebarBackground is nearly transparent. Inherited from Developer's implementation note; confirmed here as low risk.

summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied and two Documentation-Forward items tagged.
All 11 acceptance criteria are confirmed met. Architecture is clean and well-structured MVVM XAML.

Fix-Forward applied: sidebar Border upgraded from BorderThickness=0 to BorderThickness=1,0,0,0 with BorderBrush=MaterialDesignDivider — provides a 1px left-edge visual separator between the diff list and the sidebar. Non-behavioral; QA validation remains intact.

No blocking issues found. The five-card sidebar pattern is readable and appropriately scoped for the current feature surface. Inline card markup (vs. a DataTemplate-driven ItemsControl) is the right choice at this scale — five distinct Visibility bindings with different Background brushes would not simplify with a template without significant ViewModel restructuring.

comments.note: Sidebar Border: changed BorderThickness from '0' to '1,0,0,0' and added BorderBrush='{DynamicResource MaterialDesignDivider}'. Provides a subtle left-edge visual separator between the diff list (column 0) and the guidance sidebar (column 1). Without this, the only visual boundary was the Margin='8,0,0,0' gap — in dark or high-contrast themes the semi-transparent GuidanceSidebarBackground (#0AFFFFFF) is nearly invisible, leaving the two regions visually merged. Non-behavioral change; no test assertions are affected.

The 260px sidebar column width (Grid.Row=2, ColumnDefinition Width='260') is a magic number. In WPF there is no lightweight GridLength resource mechanism that avoids boilerplate, so the inline literal is acceptable for a single-view pattern. If this sidebar layout is adopted in a second view in a future plan, the value should be extracted to a shared resource to avoid drift. No action required now.

The No Changes card (lines 488–512) is the only sidebar card with no explicit Background brush — it inherits the MaterialDesign card default. The other four cards all carry explicit DiffBrush.Guidance*Background values. The asymmetry is intentional (neutral state = neutral card) but could confuse a future contributor adding a new card who may not realize the omission was deliberate. A comment on the card element (e.g., '<!-- Intentionally no Background: neutral state uses MD card default -->') would make the intent self-documenting without requiring a new brush key. Tagged as documentation-forward below.

Icon Foreground values (#EF5350, #FF9800, #9C27B0, #66BB6A) are raw hex literals repeated across both the sidebar card headers and the ListView item-style DataTriggers (lines 254, 260, 271, 275). These are consistent and correct today, but if risk-color semantics change, a file-wide find-and-replace is needed. Extracting these to named SolidColorBrush resources in DiffBrushes.xaml (e.g., DiffBrush.RemovedForeground, DiffBrush.InsertedForeground) would centralize color ownership. Low priority — the current duplication is contained within a single file and the color values match the DiffBrush alpha variants, so the intent is clear.

[documentation-forward] The sidebar column fixed width (260px) and the reasoning behind it (fits 5 cards at current copy length, preserves diff list at MinWidth=720) should be noted in the API surface documentation or a dedicated XAML architecture note. Future contributors expanding card content (longer risk copy, action links, bullet lists) need to know 260px was an intentional sizing decision, not an arbitrary default.

[documentation-forward] The No Changes materialDesign:Card (lines 488–512) intentionally omits a Background brush to use the MD card default (neutral/no-risk visual treatment). This deliberate omission should be documented — either with an inline XAML comment on the card element or a note in the component documentation — so future contributors do not assume it was accidentally missed when comparing it to the four risk-level cards that all have explicit DiffBrush.Guidance*Background values.
